column2: Core benchmark workflows were completed and stabilized across `run`, `compare`, `pack`, and `report`. The backend adapter model stayed clean, artifact generation became reviewer-friendly, and unit-test coverage improved confidence late in the cycle.
column3: Reviewer-facing materials lagged behind the engineering work. Smoke validation breadth across all backends and rates was lighter than planned, and live-mode verification depended on credentials and environment readiness.
column4: Freeze the review surface earlier, standardize a short pre-review checklist, use benchmark-pack outputs as the default review narrative, and reserve a dedicated polish pass after feature completion.
column5: Schedule a focused polish sprint immediately after feature completion, rerun one synthetic and one dataset compare across all three backends before review checkpoints, and package review documents with the latest benchmark outputs.

column2: Sprint reviewed: March 12, 2026. Team assessment: the project is almost complete, with only finishing work, regression breadth, and review packaging left before final sign-off.
column3: Main challenge: the product reached feature completeness slightly ahead of the supporting review collateral, creating last-mile pressure on polish and presentation.
column4: Improvement theme: move from feature completion to review readiness with a clearer definition of done and better sequencing for documentation.
